title: Six possibilities for locally sampled uniform symmetric distributions
formal: Resolved affirmatively: there exists an absolute constant C such that, for every fixed locality d and ε∈(0,1), all sufficiently large n have the following property. If a d-local Boolean map on independent uniform input bits has output distribution X at total variation distance at most ε from a distribution uniform on a nonempty union of Hamming-weight layers in {0,1}ⁿ, then X is within Cε of one of the six distributions defined below.
context:
A symmetric support is a union of Hamming-weight layers. Larger layers contribute more mass because every supported string receives the same probability.

Several output coordinates may use the same random input bit. Thus the sampler is not restricted to product distributions, and a low-locality map can even generate a uniform parity class.

The output need only be close to a uniform symmetric target. The conclusion says that this output must then be close to one of six simple distributions, with only a constant-factor loss in distance.

Kane, Ostuni and Wu prove the classification in the work published at STOC 2025. All six comparison distributions themselves have exact samplers of locality at most two.
why: Classifies the ability of constant-locality classical circuits to generate uniform symmetric distributions, including approximate generation rather than only exact sampling.
status_note: Resolved by Kane, Ostuni and Wu, published at STOC 2025. The complete theorem, locality and distance conventions, absolute constant, threshold dependence and six distributions were checked against arXiv v2. This is published-theorem/model verification, not independent proof verification.

progress.text: The source conjectures the six-distribution classification and proves partial cases for supports concentrated on sublinear Hamming weights.

sentences: Each output bit of a local sampler reads only a bounded number of independent random input bits.
Suppose its output is close to a distribution uniform over a symmetric set of bit strings.
The output must then be close to one of six possibilities: two point masses, their equal mixture, two parity classes, or the whole cube.
The closeness loses only an absolute constant factor, independent of locality.
The 2023 conjecture was resolved in work published at STOC 2025.

definitions: For m,n≥1, a map f:{0,1}ᵐ→{0,1}ⁿ is d-local if each output coordinate depends on at most d input coordinates; the chosen inputs may differ between outputs and may be shared. The input Uₘ is uniform on {0,1}ᵐ, and X is the law of f(Uₘ). There is no bound on m and no algorithmic uniformity requirement across n. For nonempty S⊆{0,…,n}, let U_Sⁿ be uniform on all strings x∈{0,1}ⁿ with |x|=Σⱼxⱼ∈S: every such string, rather than every allowed weight, has the same probability. For distributions P,Q on {0,1}ⁿ, TV(P,Q)=½Σₓ|P(x)−Q(x)|. The six comparison distributions are: a point mass at 0ⁿ; a point mass at 1ⁿ; equal mass on 0ⁿ and 1ⁿ; uniform on all even-weight strings; uniform on all odd-weight strings; and uniform on the entire cube. The quantifiers in the historical claim are ∃C>0 ∀d≥0 ∀ε∈(0,1) ∃n₀(d,ε) ∀n≥n₀ ∀m≥1 ∀d-local f ∀nonempty S: TV(f(Uₘ),U_Sⁿ)≤ε implies min_D TV(f(Uₘ),D)≤Cε, where D ranges over those six distributions. The result actually allows the threshold n₀ to depend only on d. No symmetry of f or of its output distribution is assumed.
answer_criterion: The affirmative resolution is Theorem 4.1 of Kane, Ostuni and Wu, which proves the stated robust six-distribution classification, with an absolute multiplicative constant. Theorem 1.2 explicitly identifies this as the resolution of the Filmus–Leigh–Riazanov–Sokolov conjecture.
